author: Adam Jones, Ph.D.
attribution: Photo: Adam Jones, Ph.D., CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Street_Scene_with_Baghdad-Mosul_Signs_-_Erbil_-_Iraq.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Large Erbil roadside direction sign; target is the LEFT column (left-turn arrow). Kirkuk is written with Arabic kaf (final ك has the inner mark), so ك is used throughout that panel; medial kaf in پاركی is visually ambiguous. The middle (Mosul / Parliament / Erbil international airport / Saad Abdulla Hall) and right (Ainkawa) columns are distractors. Car plate and pedestrians are incidental.
source_title: File:Street Scene with Baghdad-Mosul Signs - Erbil - Iraq.jpg

lines.latin: Mozey Ristin w Chinini Kurdewari (Museum of Kurdish spinning and weaving)

notes: Painted direction board (red left arrow) at Erbil citadel; target is the RIGHT sign. Dry twigs hang over the Kurdish line; no diacritic mark is visible under the ر of رستن, so it is transcribed as plain ر. Arabic line ends with dotless ى. The left sign 'أنتيك القلعة / ANTIQ KALA' is a distractor.

author: Jeffrey Beall
attribution: Photo: Jeffrey Beall, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/31437555@N00/12457397445. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/. Unmodified original.

lines.latin: Holi Shehid Se'd 'Ebdulla (Martyr Saad Abdulla Hall)

notes: Overhead gantry direction sign in Erbil (down-right arrow), close and sharp; trilingual English / Sorani Kurdish / Arabic. Diacritics as seen: ڵ (v above) in نێودەوڵەتی; plain ل in هۆلی and the first lam of عەبدولڵا, with the v mark only over the final lam-alef. Medial kaf in فرۆکە is visually ambiguous (ک/ك). Kurdistan flag and airplane pictograms; traffic light below is a distractor. Different panel and text from the roadside version in c22188447.
